method: One persistent independently reset reference process; documented ordinary controller requests and actual screenshots only. Native frames are actual response sums. Integer camera candidates are image registration, not emulator telemetry.
scope: Initial inventory of post-midpoint genuine death and respawn scenes. No uniform midpoint or activation threshold is inferred.

unresolved: Activation thresholds require controlled before/after death branches.
Untested levels and subareas remain unmeasured.
A visible standing respawn identifies a screen pose; logical feet208 uses the previously established one-pixel artwork convention.
Image registration can have aliases and unknown map fragments; alternative candidates and residuals are retained.

declaredTolerances.activationAcceptance: Inferred activation must separate the stationary negative upper position bound and a positive branch; exact threshold within the retained interval remains unmeasured.

registrationCorrection: An initial analysis mistakenly treated noncontiguous metatile descriptor IDs as atlas indices. It was corrected to use graphics-manifest.json rectangles before accepting final registrations; camera winners were unchanged and residuals fell substantially.
limits: A repeated timed-out branch can cross an unsampled life intro inside a coarse neutral batch. Its return scene and timer reset are observed, but intro/death timing is not claimed exact.

A falling player can move after its last completely matchable image below the bottom edge. Do not treat a last-visible X as a full physical maximum; stationary timeout branches provide the stronger negative bounds.
Camera-page activation is a useful hypothesis; the runtime uses explicit inferred world-X candidates and does not claim a native camera rule.
Other measured respawns are not assigned invented uniform activation thresholds.
World8-1 returns to its opening castle after the tested late death; this does not prove that no still-later checkpoint exists.
